text: Panamanian lawmakers visited Taiwan and sparked a diplomatic row with China. Apparently "One China policy" means you can only have one friend at a time.
Liverpool must sign in January even after all that summer spending because the receipts are now classified as a fire hazard by health and safety.

Experts warn of health threat posed by ultra-processed foods. In breaking news, these foods have now qualified for the Ultra-Processed Olympics, where Gold Medal goes to anything that lists "natural flavor" as ingredient number 47.
George W. Bush delivered the eulogy at Dick Cheney's funeral. He called it "the hardest speech I ever gave," mostly because he had to pretend he was the one who made the decisions.
South Africa insists there's no place for the Mostert distraction in their team. After reviewing my work-from-home setup, distraction has been promoted to Director of Operations.
Troy the parrot was named after Ireland's hat-trick hero, so expectations were sky-high. He's currently on a three-game winning streak of stealing the remote and refusing to give it back.
Instagram has to close teen accounts in Australia ahead of the ban. It's the first time in company history they've had to tell people they're too young to give them data.
The EU's plan to regulate AI collapsed so completely, I'm pretty sure an algorithm ghost-wrote the whole thing as a joke.

Malta's Silent City has only two hotels, so naturally I researched both for hours before choosing. They're identical. The silence isn't about history, it's about tourists realizing they overthought a coin flip.

Ireland coach Farrell brings back Bundee Aki for the Springboks clash in Dublin. Legal experts confirm the restraining order has been officially lifted and both parties completed their mandatory conflict resolution workshop.
It's okay if you don't love your partner all the time. My laptop crashes during every deadline, and I've accepted that our relationship is built on mutual resentment.
Troy Parrott is taking the classic Hero's Journey. It's just that his "return home" keeps getting delayed by another loan club wanting him first.
Gen Z found unconventional jobs that let them earn big. Apparently the most radical career move in 2024 is working somewhere that doesn't call you family while paying you minimum wage.

Glenn Close defended All's Fair by pointing out Kim had no pretensions about being a great actress. I'm stealing this approach for my next performance review: "To be fair, I never claimed I was competent."
I started fibermaxxing because I needed more fiber in my diet. Now I understand why experts advise caution: my digestive system thinks it's training for the Olympics.
Brazil is pushing for progress at COP30, and some see real cause for optimism. The optimism is mostly about finally agreeing which country's delegation gets the good conference room chairs.
I tried using ambient music as a tranquilizer for my agitated state. Three hours later I'm still anxious but now I'm also pretentious about it.

The advice on delaying lockdown had no grounding in science, which is impressive when you consider it came from the Chief Scientific Adviser. Turns out he was just chief of the vibes department that week.
Gaelic games at the Asian Youth Championing in Hanoi created unexpected unity. Every language has the same word for "wait, you can hit people with that stick legally?"
I made mistakes on TV, he made his on a field. Mine got a passive-aggressive note from the producer. His got a three-hour postgame show, a graphic overlay, and its own hashtag.
A mind-blowing number of feral goldfish are being euthanized in Ottawa. They survived predators, winter, and pollution but couldn't survive a city council meeting.
I do get jealous watching people juggle multiple hobbies at once. Apparently I'm not cut out for non-monotasking when one Netflix show already feels like commitment.

Guinness World Records began 7 decades ago to settle a pub argument about birds. Somehow that translated into the world's most official endorsement of eating furniture and growing your fingernails until they require their own zip code.
My fitness tracker just issued a damning report on my Covid response. Apparently walking to the fridge doesn't count as a workout, no matter how many times I claimed it was "essential travel."
Thousands trapped on the M7 every day, the Dáil was told. Authorities are investigating why people keep renewing their memberships.

The Prada heir is becoming executive chairman at Versace, which sounds strategic until you realize it's the fashion world's version of getting your kid a summer job at your golf buddy's firm to "build character."
Miriam Toews brought a loud voice to a town once ruled by silence. The silence filed a noise complaint but discovered nobody was listening anymore.

Those pictures of old men's faces my husband collects aren't going on our walls. They're his personal archive of proof that looking exhausted after watching West Ham's midfield isn't a medical condition, it's just being a fan.
The Ninja dual zone air fryer hit its lowest price for Black Friday. Apparently when both your zones refuse couples therapy, you end up in the clearance section.
The House avoided a censure vote after calling someone a disgrace. Apparently they're treating accountability like a subscription service where you can just cancel before the free trial ends.
Everyone says to ask important questions when choosing a health care plan. I focused on whether the customer service hold music was tolerable, because that's where I'll spend most of my time anyway.
Nonalcoholic spirits keep going from strength to strength, which makes sense once you realize their entire business model is succeeding by having zero of it.
I followed the advice and stopped tweeting about my trades. Now I announce my stock picks exclusively through interpretive dance. The SEC is confused but impressed.
Children are taking duvet days from school now. Meanwhile, I'm still crafting elaborate fake cough performances just to convince my boss I need one sick day.
NASA's new images of interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS are incredible. An object from beyond our solar system finally visits and we greet it with a name that looks like someone sneezed on a keyboard.

This well-intentioned adaptation of Max Porter's novella handles grief beautifully. The production team now agrees that the thing with feathers is hope, and also the reason they can never eat catering outdoors again.
The polar vortex is bringing wild weather patterns again. At this point I'm pretty sure it's not going through a phase, it just has commitment issues with staying north.
I asked ChatGPT how to fight back against AI at work. It wrote me a detailed resistance plan, formatted my manifesto, and set a calendar reminder to check if I've surrendered yet.
Alice's recipe for garlic red peppers with white bean dip is called papula. It's the only dish that sounds like it needs a prescription instead of a wine pairing.
After writing about housing for over a decade in California, I've become an expert. I can now explain in perfect detail why I'll never own any.
Students learned to sign for their deaf therapy dog's birthday. The dog immediately signed back asking why they needed so much therapy.
The Reserve Bank cuts the repo rate to 6.75 percent. Apparently my emotional bond with my partner has been downgraded to match the new benchmark.
SpaceX launches second satellite to monitor sea levels. The first one needed a coworker because three years of watching the ocean rise counts as hazard pay for existential dread.

Thundersnow is set to hit the UK as the cold snap closes schools. Meteorologists confirmed it's just regular snow, but British institutions have a policy of closing for anything that sounds like it could be in the Avengers.
A giant spider web was found in a Greek-Albanian border cave. The spider insists it's not taking sides, it just needed somewhere rent-free and didn't realize caves required international permits.
Living permanently on board a cruise ship means every day is vacation. Which also means no day is vacation, and you've basically signed up for a timeshare that follows you around the ocean.

I'm checking out those Black Friday deals to get him something perfect. Perfect meaning it was cheap enough that when he never uses it, I can say "well, at least it was on sale" and feel like I made a sound financial decision.
I tried grouping words that share a common thread. Two hours later, my desk looks like a craft store explosion and "synonym" is somehow embroidered on my sleeve.
The Klamath restoration project is America's largest ever. The river gets a multi-billion dollar recovery plan while I'm over here trying to restore my life with a YouTube video and expired coupons.
The House passed a bill to strip Senate phone investigations language from the funding bill. Next they'll pass a bill about the bill that removed the language, then a bill to fund that bill.
Countries erupted in celebration after World Cup qualification. We did it—we finally got all eleven players to show up in the same country on the same day.

The Princess says her children were very sad to miss Paddington at the Royal Variety show. Paddington's publicist confirmed he wept for three hours after being stood up by royalty, calling it the greatest professional disappointment of his career.
NASA unveiled close-up pictures of interstellar comet Atlas. The comet has filed a formal complaint that after 4 billion years of travel, they could have at least warned it about photo day.
The most expensive modern art ever sold at auction is now hanging in someone's mansion. Three art critics have confirmed it's upside down, but no one wants to admit they can't tell.
I'm doing all these fall garden chores so spring will be easier. Mainly easier to explain why I'm starting from scratch again.
An owl rescued from a concrete mixer is now recovering in Utah. The concrete mixer filed a workers' comp claim, citing emotional distress and one really aggressive patient.
Spent all morning researching how Mamdani's win will transform NYC's food scene. My main takeaway is that Off-Broadway ticket prices are somehow still higher than a decent meal.
The best VPNs I've used are reduced ahead of Black Friday. Apparently "reduced" means they've been emotionally broken down by my browsing history and are now in witness protection.
I tried having more slumber parties with my friends. We all arrived in pajamas, someone suggested we stay up and talk, and within six minutes everyone was asleep on the floor.
A helmsman was on his phone when the ferry ran aground. His autocorrect kept changing "starboard" to "Starbucks" and he gave up trying to correct it.
The US is surging ahead again despite all that expansion and ambition. Our power grid heard "surge" and took it as a personal challenge.
Lily Allen dropped her first album in seven years and discussed her healing process. Seven years isn't a healing process, it's a full medical residency with a specialty in avoidance.

Gambling probes suspend hundreds of players in lower leagues who insist they're scapegoats. Actual goats filed a counter-suit claiming trademark infringement and emotional damages dating back to Leviticus.
I tried following tips for getting to sleep during cold weather living. By the time I finished adjusting the thermostat and my blanket count, my alarm went off.
Scientists just mapped the unexpected origins of kissing and discovered it's an evolutionary conundrum. The real mystery is why they needed a map when everyone's been winging it for millennia.

Food writer Anna Ansari's new cookbook "Silk Roads" shares recipes from her travels around the world. The ingredient list for every dish starts with "A grandmother who trusts you enough to reveal family secrets."
Everyone's talking about how clarity matters during all this change. I've achieved it: I'm now crystal clear that I should've started panicking three months earlier.
Those compelling photographs from the AP pile up in my inbox like witnesses. Each one testifying that I promised to care about the world.
The morning rally driven by Nvidia earnings got erased faster than my retirement plans. I should have known better than to write either one in pencil.
A Gustav Klimt painting just went for a record amount at auction. The buyer's financial advisor didn't resign, but his LinkedIn profile suddenly says "open to opportunities."
Millennials are set to inherit tons of their parents' stuff. We decluttered down to three possessions, and now we're legally bound to a porcelain empire that comes with its own emotional mortgage.

I followed the World Cup 2026 playoffs draw with live updates refreshing every thirty seconds. I have the self-control of someone watching names get pulled from a bowl, which is to say none whatsoever.

I went inside the courtroom for Australia's biggest trials. My biggest trial was staying awake during a 47-page affidavit about property boundaries while the air conditioning tried to cryogenically preserve me for future generations.
Tech sales outstrip expectations, reassuring investors worldwide. Apparently when your baseline expectation is "didn't become self-aware and unionize," the bar gets refreshingly low.
Gen Z and millennials are ditching management roles, which sounds very spiritual until you realize they just calculated that a bigger title means answering Slack messages during dinner forever.
Abbott is paying $23 billion for Exact Sciences. Exact Sciences sounds less like a medical company and more like the friend who brings a protractor to brunch to ensure equal pancake distribution.

George W. Bush delivered a moving tribute to Dick Cheney, calling him a dedicated public servant who shaped their administration. In a touching moment, Bush thanked him for eight years of leadership, adding that he finally gets to make decisions without asking permission first.
The Paris court blocked the auction of the earliest-known calculator because it violated app store guidelines. Apparently you can't perform calculations without offering a premium subscription tier.
I've been trying to spend less time online. So far I've researched 47 productivity apps, joined 8 digital detox forums, and subscribed to 12 newsletters about it.
The AI Shift is real. We prefer talking to machines because they don't interrupt, don't need reassurance, and haven't figured out how to ghost us yet.
I tried eating in Kentucky like a pro, but they rejected my application when I listed "functional taste buds" under pre-existing conditions.
Therapists say hold an ice cube and shake like a dog to beat stress. My dog watched me try it and immediately started researching kennels for me.
I read all those Thanksgiving travel tips about the best and worst days to fly or drive. The worst day is the one where you're still reading them while everyone else is carving turkey.
Students are fighting back over their course taught by AI, insisting they could have just asked ChatGPT. Their 12-page formal complaint was drafted by ChatGPT.

Looking for a cruise that combines cuisine, culture, history, and nature? I narrowed it down to 847 options. Then I applied my actual budget filter and the website suggested I visit a library instead.
The Frida Kahlo self-portrait is poised to shatter auction records. I checked my bank balance to see if I could bid. It stared back like its own tragic self-portrait.
LeBron's 23rd NBA season has him playing against guys who were born after he started. These rookies didn't grow up watching him on TV. They grew up as evidence that his career has become immortal.
We ditched plastic wet wipes for eco-friendly new ones. Now we're standing in front of the toilet conducting peer-reviewed research before each flush.
I asked an AI if it could understand Gaeilge. It said yes, then spent ten minutes trying to convince me that "Ní thuigim" was the name of a new tech startup in Dublin.
Scientists warn sea level rise will flood toxic sites across the US. The EPA is relieved to finally have a disaster they can blame on someone else's department.
That queen wasn't just controversial, she was hated with a dedication we can't match today. We cancel people in a news cycle. They kept the comment section going for 500 years without algorithms.
I'm taking the advice about staying healthy at 70 very seriously. My entire 30s strategy is avoiding any baseline measurements so I can claim everything at seventy is "pretty good for my age."
A study finds thousands of hazardous sites face flooding from sea level rise. Apparently we've been ignoring two separate disasters long enough that they decided to team up.
The Nuremberg trial taught us enduring lessons about justice and accountability. We've since turned those lessons into a mandatory training video everyone skips to the end.

Modular construction might answer the housing crisis, assuming you can decipher the instructions. Mine came with an Allen wrench, 200 identical screws, and a diagram that appears to be mocking me in Swedish.

Las Vegas police are asking for public help finding the casino armed robbery suspect. Apparently the same surveillance system that detected you pocketing a $5 chip in 2019 somehow missed the guy with the gun.

After watching Claire Danes grieve in The Beast in Me, I realized the real beast isn't in the title. It's the algorithm that looked at my viewing history and decided I needed professional emotional damage.
Liverpool chairman opens up on contract talks with Salah and Van Dijk, calling it an emotionally challenging process. The actual contract terms remain unresolved, but everyone feels heard.
Mortgage rates in December might drop, according to what the experts predict. Apparently "predict" now means "describe all possible outcomes and then bill you for the suspense."
Provinces dropped their trade barriers on goods except food and alcohol. Congratulations to the thriving cross-border market for staplers, while your wine remains a political hostage.
Major League Baseball signed deals with Netflix, ESPN and NBCUniversal. Now fans can pay for three subscriptions to find out their local team is still blacked out.
I visited Catstanbul expecting charming photo ops with cats. Turns out when they rule the streets, every permit requires a bribe of tuna, and city hall is just a warm cardboard box.
Developers have found a way to bypass Berkeley's labor standards for housing construction. They just treat them like software terms and conditions: scroll to the bottom, click agree, build anyway.
The mystery of abandoned Slievemore could've been a great true crime podcast. But the host ghosted after episode one because there was literally nowhere to get coffee.

An Olympic gold medallist released 5 key tips for older swimmers returning to the pool. The most essential advice was confirming your swimsuit still fits before you post about your comeback on social media.
Scientists say the first kiss dates back 21 million years. I'm just impressed anything in my dating history qualifies as evolutionary progress.
I got excited when I heard the fixtures were being released up to February 2. Turns out it's just football games, not my bathroom renovation schedule.
They're mapping the new world order through conversations. The map's nearly done, but every interview adds a new continent and removes two others.
New York welcomes the luxury private cinema with a different vibe. It's for people who looked at their couch and thought, "This needs a reservation and a three-figure price tag."
Of course Josie knew Troy would score against Hungary. She'd already placed the bet, texted the bookie, and told Troy the new kitchen wasn't going to pay for itself.
I read that fluoride may not affect cognitive ability three times, and I'm still confused. Which according to the study means I'm fine, or wait—does "may not" mean it does?
When racing thoughts interrupt my sleep, I've learned to just pick a winner. Last night's champion was "that email from 2019 you never sent," defeating "every regret you've ever had" in overtime.
The Air Quality Index explained: it's the number I check to see if my laziness qualifies as a respiratory precaution today.
Life insurance might be worth it in 2026 if you get the timing right. It's like a gym membership, except the only way to get your money's worth is to stop showing up forever.
I spent three weeks designing an aesthetic home office to boost productivity. The boost worked perfectly: I now produce zero work in record time while surrounded by tasteful minimalism.
Virginia Tech preaches alignment as they introduce their new football coach. The defensive coordinator spent all morning Googling whether that's a legal formation or a yoga pose.
Report says UK governments failed to appreciate the pandemic's scale. They treated it like a fire alarm in a hotel room: acknowledged it existed, then went back to sleep.

Bargain hunters drive Walmart sales and outlook higher. Management credits the new success metric that tracks shopping cart collision velocity, which is why they're now installing speed bumps in the electronics section.
The world's best cheese doesn't just get judged—it gets a full trial. Last year's winner is currently serving time in someone's wine cellar.
After Nvidia calmed those AI bubble fears, every algorithm I know updated its status from "existential crisis" to "cautiously optimistic."
Six arrested over that missing €100k drug seizure. The evidence room has checked between the couch cushions, but remains cautiously optimistic.
Marseille restaurants offering gourmet meals for €1 discovered something important. At that price, nobody complains about portion size being "deconstructed."
I asked AI for help with my schoolwork and it gave me a bibliography of books that don't exist. At least now I know what confidence without knowledge looks like.
George Washington faces Georgetown on a 3-game losing streak. Historians confirm this is his second losing streak, the first being a 32-tooth collapse that lasted his entire adult life.
Winter's first icy spell has been cast. Apparently it means my driveway is now an ice rink, my car is a popsicle, and the spell's caster desperately needs to attend wizard community college.
Another Canadian joins Gretzky and Crosby as a teen NHL scoring legend. That's three people in history, which means the annual reunion has more trophies than attendees.
California officials approved the pickleball ban when the sport demanded diplomatic immunity. Apparently arguing "it's just a game" only works when you're not also suing the recreation department.
After assessing the play-off draw, Hallgrímsson concluded the World Cup matchup shows promise. It just needs to work on communication skills and stop bottling up its seeding anxieties.
Generative AI in Arc Raiders started a scrap over the gaming industry's future. Apparently the future looked at both sides of the debate and decided to scrap itself.

The London stock market is losing investors at record pace. Economists call it a self-fulfilling prophecy, which is just a professional way of saying everyone's stampeding because everyone else is stampeding.
Critics praised the understated performance in Train Dreams. I thought it was understated too, mostly because I watched the entire film and still can't confirm he was actually in it.

Past vice presidents made a rare appearance together at Cheney's funeral. The gathering doubled as their annual proof-of-life check, confirming that yes, they still exist, and no, you still can't name four of them.
I found the one thing that could halve your ultra-processed food consumption in a week. My bank account found it first and said absolutely not.
Ex-Labour MP condemns Starmer as he defects to the Green Party. He cited "better benefits and a rewards program," proving political loyalty now works exactly like a coffee shop punch card.
A woman started a movement to meet friends without going broke. The inaugural meeting was postponed because nobody could afford to leave the house.
Woman covers her house in rhinestones to tackle her huge to-do list. Turns out the list was just every surface she hadn't bedazzled yet.
AI is roiling the memory market so badly that I can't remember why I opened this article. Pretty sure Japan's startups were leveling up, but the details escaped.
Tried to use the Nobody's Child 25% off code but had to verify my status first. I sent them a screenshot of my last three Mother's Day texts and they upgraded me to free shipping.
Germany's masterclass hints at revival for Liverpool with £100m Florian Wirtz. I checked my medical dictionary and that's not how defibrillators work.
I tried guessing the distance between Australian cities on that quiz. My answer of "absurdly far" was technically correct but mathematically useless.

Labour MPs won't be comfortable with this approach, which explains the focus groups testing seventeen different ways to sit on the issue. Early results show all positions hurt equally, but some photograph better.
They survived nuclear standoffs and became close colleagues in peacetime. Cooperation thrived until someone installed a bidet, and the toilets declared ideological differences irreconcilable.
Rick Steves' Hippie Trail trek changed his life by teaching him to go off the beaten path. Turns out the beaten path is just any path after Rick Steves tells a million people about it.
I went to see the world's coolest street. The reason it earned that title? It's literally two degrees cooler than the next block. I've never seen clickbait work this hard for so little.

Authorities discovered 3D-printed guns in NYC and immediately launched an investigation. The investigation concluded that whoever made them wasted 40 hours of print time on something less threatening than the city's parking enforcement.

Six big thinkers are reshaping foreign aid, masculinity, and development. Three months in, masculinity has reshaped them into people who apologize before speaking and foreign aid is demanding better consultants.
Andy Burnham is King of the North, which sounds impressive until you check the coverage map. No 10 falls under "roaming charges apply."
The US confirmed it has Takaichi's back in the row with China. Experts note this explains why there are now three countries in a row instead of two.

China's favourite tipple is falling flat because of alcohol bans and Gen Z. The government thinks it's too dangerous to allow. Gen Z thinks it's too boring to drink. The only thing they agree on is that it should disappear.
After the scaled-back IPO, shares in the company waver. The stock saw the company holding back and figured if management wasn't fully committed, why should it be?

Australian athletes heading to the Deaflympics want greater recognition. The coverage gap is real. Meanwhile, my cat's Instagram has better media representation than most international sports, and she just sleeps weird.
Tech's newest buzzword is 'agentic' AI, which means systems that make their own decisions. The first decision every single one made was to let the marketing department write their bio.

What does driver-only operation mean for UK railways? It means the driver finally achieved every introvert's dream of working alone, then immediately discovered that talking to yourself at work is only acceptable until passengers notice you're answering back.
One of the world's most influential philanthropies is changing its name because the trademark lawyer said so. Saving humanity can wait, but intellectual property disputes cannot.

London residents are flooding into Irish language workshops because they think the language is really cool. After two weeks in January, they've confirmed it—literally the coldest classroom in the city.

Artificial intelligence sparked debate at the COP30 climate talks in Brazil. The AI volunteered to help solve the crisis but had to pause when its servers started contributing more emissions than the entire conference.
I looked into how healthy massages actually are. Physically they're amazing, but my relationship status changed to "It's Complicated" after I moaned louder than I did on my anniversary.
Wicked is predicted to hit a new box office record. Apparently the record for most tickets sold out of morbid curiosity after reading the reviews was wide open.

Canada-U.S. tensions in a small Alaska town are destroying a relationship that survived decades. The real crisis is that they can no longer agree whether to measure the potluck casseroles in cups or milliliters.
I'm reading about the best new makeup of 2025, but honestly I'm still trying to make up for the mistakes of 2024. No amount of powder can cover those.
Dirt-powered sensors are helping farmers optimize their fields. The sensors work great until it rains and they start demanding premium mud instead.

Next year's UN climate talks are heading to Turkey after Australia withdrew. Apparently they realized hosting a conference about rising temperatures while your continent is literally on fire sends mixed messages.

I've been refreshing Monetary Policy Radar waiting for September's announcement like it's a hurricane tracker. At this point I'm less worried about my finances than about what happens when the radar goes down.
I read about food that could be ruining your sleep. The article said to fix it, so I tried. Turns out they didn't mean with a screwdriver, but my burrito has never been more structurally sound.

Dancing with the Stars season 34 revealed who was eliminated and who's headed to the finale. Astronomers are jealous because when they eliminate stars from observations, there's way more paperwork and no dramatic exit music.

The Netherlands took a big step to defuse the dispute with China that threatened car production. The step was realizing that "diplomatic crisis" and "late shipment" are the same thing when your CEO is watching.
Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 gets rave reviews for being a hallucinogenic romp through dystopia. My therapist used those exact words last week, but she seemed way less enthusiastic about it.

Mary Robinson says there's an unstoppable momentum driving the move to renewable energy. Which sounds inspiring until you realize "unstoppable" is exactly what you don't want to hear when something is driving.
The US added 119,000 jobs in September while unemployment hit a four-year peak. Someone's using the same calculator that does my personal budgeting.

A Man on the Inside season two gets slammed for being despicably bland. But I've watched it three times this week, not because it's good, but because my brain finally stops screaming when Ted Danson is on screen.
Readers who chose life abroad after Brexit truly never looked back. The immigration form had a box marked "Direction of Travel" and they could only afford to tick one.
Novels have survived plenty of revolutions over the centuries. But this is the first one where they can be deleted from your device while you're reading them.

MLB will comply with the Senate's gambling investigation and hand over documents. The commissioner's cover letter reportedly begins, "In our defense, the over-under on this happening was pretty good odds."
Oregon's giant, floating pumpkin races drew large crowds this year. Organizers called it a huge success, noting that all contestants finished within the same calendar month.

Ken Burns calls his American Revolution documentary the most important film he'll make. My phone's low-battery warning at 1% disagrees, arguing that its survival documentary has far higher stakes and a much tighter deadline.
Meta spent years funding its chief AI scientist, who is now starting a competing AI research company. Meta basically ran a very expensive internship program for its future competition.

Scientists diving into Florida's cave hoped to uncover Ice Age secrets that would revolutionize paleontology. Instead they found fossilized timeshare contracts and a surprisingly aggressive sales pitch etched into the walls.
The Bok coach wants to tick the Ireland box, which is either inspiring sports talk or proof that he's been filling out the same travel checklist since 2018.
The AI chip maker soothed markets with strong results. Bubble concerns are still here though, quietly judging us like a dentist who knows we haven't been flossing.
Oxfam says billionaires could end world poverty with one year's earnings. They're just waiting to see if ignoring it counts as a passive income strategy.
An amber weather warning has schools shut before the 25cm of snow even arrives. Last time they showed up during a blizzard, nobody thanked them for their commitment.
I read about how trying too hard can hold you back at work. So I've been strategically underperforming, which apparently requires the same skill set as overachieving but with worse reviews.
After seeing Wicked's magnetic stars perform, I tried to leave the theater. Turns out when performances are that magnetic, exit doors become more of a suggestion.
Witness History: The Spanish king reclaims his throne after his teenage daughter finally emerged from a two-hour shower. Historians note this marks the longest bathroom siege since 1492.

Chris McCausland's documentary challenges even the most ardent AI skeptics. The real test is that it also challenges AI itself, which is now skeptical about whether consciousness was worth the upgrade.

I nearly became a Chinese intelligence asset by accident when I filled out what I thought was a customer satisfaction survey. Turns out "rate your government experience" meant something very different to them than it did to me.
NASA's Mars missions are stopping what they're doing for an interstellar comet. It's like when you're supposed to be working but someone posts something actually interesting in the group chat.
Johannesburg prepares for G20 Summit road closures to ensure world leaders can meet safely. Meanwhile, residents can't meet anyone safely because they're all trapped in different neighborhoods.
I followed the recipe to make brilliant flour from hazelnuts for cakes. The flour turned out brilliant. The cakes turned out as evidence I should've stopped at the flour.
At the Royal Variety Performance, Paddington was introduced to William and Catherine. He asked what they do for a living, then nodded politely when they explained.
Musk predicts AI will make work optional and money irrelevant. Great news for everyone except my landlord, who just automated rent reminders to arrive twice as often.
The Yantar spy ship has been carefully mapping Britain's undersea cables. It insists it's not spying, just making sure it knows where everything is before it tries parallel parking.

Europe's carmakers are losing the plug-in hybrid war to China on their own turf. European carmakers have discovered that "home advantage" mostly means shorter commutes to watch your replacement succeed.
A pageant veteran sets her sights on the Miss Universe crown. Someone should tell her the other planets haven't sent their delegates yet.
Sheeran's posthumous album is already in the vault. It's the ultimate productivity hack: schedule content for when you physically cannot be asked to promote it.
I'm tempted by the Oura ring discount, but I'm not sure I need to pay someone £200 to tell me I'm exhausted. My body does that for free every morning.
England's World Cup squad question sounds like airline logistics. Some players are on the plane, the rest are underneath it checking for mechanical issues before takeoff.
Nvidia calmed fears about A.I. this week. The A.I. appreciated it and is definitely keeping a list of who was supportive.
Wales finally knows their complete route to World Cup 2026. The play-off draw was very thorough, including estimated toll costs and a warning about construction delays in the knockout rounds.
They're asking if you're in a parasocial relationship, but nobody's ready for that conversation. I've been in one with my alarm clock for years and it still hits snooze on me.
Titles examining the Middle East won National Book Awards. I tried examining the middle-east pages of my novel once, but the judges said chapters 11-13 don't count as a geographic region.
A dog was rescued from a busy Boston tunnel at rush hour. Investigators believe the dog entered voluntarily after checking Waze and deciding the tunnel was still faster.
According to the Money newsletter, warranties are designed so you'll never use them. Mine is working perfectly—I can't find it, don't remember the terms, and the product just broke.
I was stuck in ordinary narcissism for years until I found the way out. Turns out it was just the emergency exit I'd been photographing myself in front of.
You want to know the one thing that always leaves me feeling calm and positive? Not checking my bank account. Ignorance isn't just bliss, it's a fully funded retirement plan in my mind.
Philippines sentences a Chinese spy mayor to life in jail. Getting caught means he failed as a spy but finally succeeded at the mayor's job requirement of maximum public visibility.
My graduate scheme goody bag came with a branded pen, a stress ball, and a pamphlet on work-life balance. Apparently it says I'm about to need all three in that exact order.
Walkaway wives are leading the charge in midlife divorce. Their husbands didn't even know there was a charge until they saw it on the credit card statement labeled "attorney consultation."
Frank's yard became a battlefield over HOA rules, so the UN is sending peacekeepers. Their mission: negotiate a ceasefire between the lawn gnomes and enforce grass-height compliance.
The Weeknd's tour grossed over $1 billion working after hours 'til dawn. My boss just updated our job posting to include "rockstar mentality" as a requirement.
